momentum.text: Election Day opened with mostly technical and weather problems (Broward County system fault ~20 min; Westchester scanner delays). Early-vote turnout ran well above 2022.
Maine on track for record midterm turnout, per Secretary of State Shenna Bellows — Maine Senate is a must-flip for Democrats.
Appeals court lets DOJ warn election officials they could be prosecuted for not following its demands on voting procedures; another ruling allows requests to segregate suspected noncitizen ballots.
Supreme Court declined the administration's emergency request to stop California from counting ~20,000 ballots DHS flagged as possible noncitizens.
Final NYT/Siena polls: Democrats lead all seven Senate toss-ups — Talarico 50–43 (TX), Jackson 51–45 (ME), Brown 49–44 (OH), Peltola 48–46 (AK), Turek 48–47 (IA).
Kalshi Senate odds for Democrats hit 74–75%, the platform's high, up from ~63% on Oct. 2. Republicans led this market as late as July (60% R peak).
Polling-error risk: 2016, 2020 and 2024 polls understated Republicans by ~3–5 pts. A miss that size likely costs Democrats the Senate and narrows the House.
momentum.source: Silver Bulletin via DC News Now

momentum.text: Cook's final governor ratings moved four races toward Democrats (incl. Wisconsin to Lean D); Cook projects a Democratic net gain of 2–4 governorships.
Cook moved 19 House races toward Democrats and none toward Republicans; Democrats now 'favored outright' in the 218 seats needed.
Trump approval at record lows (CNN/SSRS 32%); NYT/Siena generic ballot D+11, CNN D+10.
Georgia governor remains a statistical tie: Rick Jackson (R) +1.6 over Keisha Lance Bottoms (D), even as Ossoff leads by ~7 for Senate.

Mid-decade redistricting and court rulings (incl. Louisiana v. Callais narrowing VRA majority-minority protections) shifted the House map toward the GOP; one model's GOP odds rose from 18.9% to 27.2% in a week.
